state.misconception_label: Has used slant height and base to find area of a triangle rather than perpendicular height and base

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: How would you calculate the area of this triangle? ![A triangle, base 12m. All three sides are equal.](). I got \( \frac{12 \times 12}{2} \) because I added the side lengths instead of multiplying.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To calculate the area of a triangle with base 12m, you need to use the formula A = 1/2 * base * height. In this case, the height should be the perpendicular height, not the slant height. So, the correct calculation would be A = 1/2 * 12 * h. Make sure to use the perpendicular height next time.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so I need to use the perpendicular height, not just any side of the triangle. But how do I know what the perpendicular height is? Do I have to measure it, or can I work it out from the other measurements?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To find the perpendicular height of a triangle, you can use the Pythagorean theorem if you have the side lengths. Remember, the perpendicular height forms a right angle with the base. So, you can calculate it using the Pythagorean theorem or by drawing an altitude from the apex to the base.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher correctly identifies perpendicular vs. slant height but simply tells the student what to do rather than engaging with their thinking, and while the student asks a good follow-up question, they never demonstrate understanding of the original misconception or work through finding the height themselves.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently states explicit procedures (triangle area formula, Pythagorean theorem), shows the worked formula structure (A = 1/2 * 12 * h), and provides direct corrective feedback on the procedural error of using slant height instead of perpendicular height.
